strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine limitations of purely visual 3DGS SLAM under motion blur, low texture, and exposure variations
Principled three-stage IMU initialization and tight coupling of visual-inertial terms in unified optimization framework, avoiding naive fusion approaches
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four diverse datasets with detailed ablation studies, robustness analysis on strided sequences, and comparison against 13 baselines
Strong empirical results with consistent improvements in tracking accuracy, superior rendering quality, and exceptional robustness on degraded conditions (98.99% recall@10cm on stride=10)
Excellent presentation with extensive implementation details, hyperparameters, and reproducibility materials in supplementary content
Demonstrates practical impact by successfully tracking sequences where competitors fail completely
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty—primarily combines existing techniques (DROID-SLAM visual frontend + standard VI-SLAM formulation + 3DGS mapping) rather than introducing new algorithmic insights; inertial residual formulation follows established approaches from OKVIS/VINS-Mono

Significant computational efficiency concerns with 46% slower tracking speed (16.4 vs 30.6 FPS) and 43% slower overall performance than HI-SLAM2; requires high-end GPU (RTX 5090) for real-time operation; limitations acknowledged but not resolved

Incomplete comparison with directly comparable work: MM3DGS-SLAM (most relevant baseline) only evaluated on UTMM; VINGS-Mono (another recent VI+3DGS method) barely compared; inadequate fairness discussion for RGB+IMU vs RGB+LiDAR+IMU comparison

Limited evaluation scope restricted to monocular RGB+IMU; no stereo, multi-camera, fisheye support; relatively small-scale datasets (max ~1.3 km); no real-world deployment or end-to-end application demonstration

Missing analysis of when/why IMU helps most, no visualization of Gaussian map quality improvements, limited discussion of IMU bias evolution and convergence properties; design choices (L1 losses, weight selection) lack justification

Extensive hyperparameter tuning required with no sensitivity analysis; dataset-specific N_init values (20, 25, 15) suggest generalization concerns; inelegant 3-second keyframe timeout rule driven by drift concerns increases keyframe overhead
Limited failure case analysis and discussion of when/why method fails; only one extreme condition example (Figure 5) provided

strengths: Addresses practical limitation of visual-only 3DGS SLAM by tightly coupling IMU measurements; IMU ubiquity makes this well-motivated
Comprehensive experimental validation across four diverse datasets with 13 baselines, strong ablation studies, and robustness evaluation under frame drops and extreme conditions
Consistent state-of-the-art results: best or near-best tracking accuracy (ATE RMSE) across all datasets, with only method succeeding on all sequences without failure
Well-designed staged IMU initialization approach (vision-only → inertial-only → joint optimization) demonstrates principled robustness strategy
Dual evaluation metrics (tracking + rendering quality) and high-quality qualitative results (Fig. 3) demonstrate practical effectiveness for both localization and reconstruction
Clear presentation with informative system overview, proper mathematical formulations, and extensive supplementary material supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (DROID-SLAM visual tracking, standard IMU pre-integration, 3D Gaussian Splatting mapping) with incremental component contributions (staged initialization, inertial residuals, loop closure updates all represent straightforward adaptations of established methods)
Incomplete comparison with concurrent VIO+3DGS methods: MM3DGS-SLAM only evaluated on UTMM without LiDAR variant; VINGS-Mono not evaluated on most datasets; GI-SLAM mentioned but not compared

Computational efficiency concerns: runtime 7.09 FPS slower than HI-SLAM2's 12.53 FPS; acknowledged NumPy IMU implementation suggests suboptimal performance; more keyframes generated despite claimed robustness

Missing technical depth: loop closure uses simple optical flow thresholding; Gaussian updates (Eqs. 5-7) lack sophistication; no analysis of why joint optimization specifically helps; computational complexity analysis absent
Insufficient ablation studies: no comparison of staged vs. joint initialization from start; no bias modeling sensitivity analysis; no per-dataset component importance breakdown

Limited generalization scope: all experiments assume pinhole cameras (no rolling shutter); single self-captured extreme conditions sequence; small-scale indoor datasets dominate; no evaluation on large-scale outdoor exploration
Depth of limitations discussion: multi-camera/fisheye stated but not explored; Gaussian representation limitations (unbounded scenes) not addressed; failure mode analysis absent; future work vague
Reproducibility gaps: code availability not mentioned; dataset-dependent hyperparameters (N_init ∈ {15,20,25}) lack principled selection; partial NumPy implementation limits reproducibility
